title: Charles “Gene” Parks Jr. et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC denied all four complaint items concerning multiple elder resignations, pastoral severance and benefits, a plan involving about twelve months with an interim pastor, and contemplated revision of local bylaws. The Assembly adopted the judgment; a procedural dissent did not alter it.
first_summary: Complainants challenged a Session plan under which most elders voluntarily resigned, the Session granted severance and benefits to its former pastor, proposed about a year with an interim pastor before a permanent call, and contemplated revising local bylaws. The SJC denied all four items. It held that the BCO permitted jointly considered voluntary resignations, that severance concerned resignation and the budget rather than a pastoral call, and that the plan and bylaw proposal were not themselves unconstitutional. Any later call still had to follow the BCO without undue delay, and local bylaws had to remain consistent with it.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: Minutes lines 5953-5957 identify Charles “Gene” Parks Jr. et al. v. Central Carolina Presbytery as SJC Docket 92-5 and record Assembly adoption. Original case lines 64-66 identify the signed decision and SJC approval by 23 concurring votes.
evidence_notes.dispute: Original lines 18-38 identify four challenges: coordinated elder resignations, severance and insurance benefits, a plan for about twelve months before a permanent call, and contemplated bylaw revision.
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: Original lines 40-62 deny all four items. Multiple resignations were compatible with BCO 24-6 when a Session deliberated together; severance followed resignation and fell within budget authority; the plan did not itself call a pastor and permissibly contemplated interim stated supply; local bylaws were envisioned by the BCO and no intended conflict appeared.
evidence_notes.qualifications: Original line 56 requires any actual pastoral call to comply with BCO 20-2 without undue delay and limits stated supply to a year unless renewed at the Session's request and Presbytery's review. Lines 58-62 rest the bylaw result on no indicated intent to conflict with the BCO. Lines 68-72 record denial of a constitutional inquiry; lines 74-86 are a dissent about adjudicative procedure, not adopted reasoning.
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: Not applicable; the SJC decision supplies its own four judgments and reasons. The Assembly's adoption in the Minutes incorporates this same judgment rather than a different docket's decision.
